text:
jules: quick follow-up on the Triton vs CUTLASS kernel debate from the RFC thread. we need a concrete plan for: perf gaps across seq_len, fallback policy, and instrumentation for rollout. want owners + small checklist. :eyes:
priya: agree. my read: Triton wins for fast iteration and fused attention variants, CUTLASS (hand-tuned cuda kernels) still beats it for very long prefixes and when using int8 quant. memory patterns differ too (kv layout).
sam: +1. also ops-surface/ABI matters — our runtime needs a clean kernel interface so we can plug either backend without duplicating batching/cache logic.
katie: can someone summarize customer-facing impact in 1-2 bullets? will brief sales/solutions.
jules: two bullets: 1) dev-time: Triton = faster prototyping, fewer bugs in fusion; 2) infra/cost: CUTLASS may reduce token cost for high-prefix workloads (search/chat history heavy) but higher engineering maintenance.
priya: I ran quick microbenchmarks yesterday on rtx-a5000 for models with 4k vs 32k context. results: Triton ~10% faster at <=4k (fp16), CUTLASS ~15% faster at 32k (int8 path) and ~8% lower mem. I pushed logs to the perf doc: https://redwood.internal/perf/kernel-attn-bench (see table seq_len distribution).
benchbot: benchmark summary attached: mean_latency_ms: Triton@4k=12.1, CUTLASS@4k=13.4, Triton@32k=230, CUTLASS@32k=195. tail_p95 similar pattern.
sam: thanks. two follow-ups from infra side: (A) we need a runtime switch that can route by model & seq_len threshold; (B) fallback rule when a Triton kernel OOMs -> automatically route to CUTLASS or generic cuda kernel. Prefer policy config in model descriptor.
priya: agree on switch. implementation note: low-latency routing needs routing decision pre-kernel (before allocating huge kv caches). Also need telemetry hooks to capture which backend served request and cache hit rates.
jules: propose action items (compact):
- A1: define kernel-abi version + minimal API (input buffers, kv layout, workspace) — owner: sam — due: 2026-04-04
- A2: expanded perf matrix (fp16, int8, seq=[512,4k,16k,32k]) on p3/p4/trn — owner: priya + benchbot — due: 2026-03-29
- A3: runtime routing prototype (model-config flag + seq_len threshold + fallback to generic cuda) — owner: jules — due: 2026-04-11
- A4: telemetry plan (events, metrics, tag backend, kernel_name, mem_alloc, oom_count) + dashboard mock — owner: katie (PM) + sam — due: 2026-03-31
- A5: small safety test-suite (OOM, perf-regression, bit-exactness where possible) — owner: priya — due: 2026-04-08

katie: tidy list, thanks. i'll coordinate the customer impact note once we have the perf matrix.
priya: one more technical callout: CUTLASS kernels currently require a slightly different kv layout (interleaved vs planar) to reach perf. that means our loader needs to optionally transform on pinning. cost of transform needs measurement (should include in A2).
sam: implementation detail for A1: let's keep ABI agnostic to memory format: expose a 'transform_hint' and let kernels opt into zero-copy if layout matches. prevents runtime copying unless necessary.
jules: good. also, can we cap the number of in-flight routing policies? i.e., prefer model-level pinned backend with global override for emergencies. keep policy simple.
priya: adding to A2: measure transform latency for 4k/32k and include mem overhead.
benchbot: queued jobs: a2-int8-32k, a2-fp16-4k, transform-latency-4k. ETA 6h.
jules: final ask: everyone please drop a :thumbsup: once you accept ownership or suggest a new owner. i'll compile a short RFC follow-up doc after owners ack and link to rollout plan.
sam: ack for A1 :thumbsup:
priya: ack for A2/A5 :thumbsup:
katie: ack for A4 :thumbsup:
jules: noted. I'll create the follow-up doc and PR the model-config schema change. link will be posted here. :rocket:
